messages:
ops-bot: [ALERT] PRODUCTION kv-cache continuous-batching ramp detected in prod-us-west-2 — eviction rate spiking, p95 token latency rising, sending page to oncall
jamie: copying. seeing evictions on 4/6 pods for kv-cache-shard-3, OOM-ish behavior in arena allocator logs
devin: i’m 1st oncall, joining now. which service alerts?
anya: embeddings-service and gen-api surfaces errors, customers 3xx -> 5xx increase reported via cs
maria-cs: FYI: two enterprise customers reported degraded throughput ~12:40 PDT, they see timeouts. holding them until we have root cause
jamie: grabbing logs from pod kvcache-3b2, tailing allocator: ```
2026-03-15T19:39:12Z  [arena] alloc failed: cudaMalloc returned cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
2026-03-15T19:39:13Z  [kv-cache] slab_fragmentation=0.78 free_slots=120 used_slots=4820
2026-03-15T19:39:14Z  [batcher] batch_size=64 -> dynamic growth to 384 due to continuous batching mis-shape
```
devin: that batch growth is our suspect — continuous-batching policy bumped batches under a new distribution, causing many large KV slots to be held -> fragmentation
ops-bot: triggered runbook: kv-cache-frag-oncall.runbook -> paging devin, jamie, anya
anya: can we throttle batching or pin a max_batch_size quickly? we have a config switch in platform-config-store
leo: i can flip a runtime flag. recommended immediate action: set CONTBATCH_MAX_TOKENS=2048 and CONTBATCH_MAX_ITEMS=32 for prod-us-west-2
devin: please apply to route: embeddings-prod-us-west-2 first (highest customer impact) then gen-api
leo: applying now via deploy-tool: ```
curl -XPOST https://platform-config/api/v1/overrides \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -d '{"service":"embeddings-prod-us-west-2","overrides":{"CONTBATCH_MAX_TOKENS":"2048","CONTBATCH_MAX_ITEMS":"32"}}'
```
leo: response: 200 OK, change rolled to 6/6 proxies (rolling)
jamie: monitoring evictions and allocator logs. p95 token latency baseline 120ms before, now 210ms during surge
anya: also put a temporary KV cache eviction-priority change to prefer small-slot evictions to reduce fragmentation; will push a canary to one shard
devin: agree, do canary on shard-1 then scale if stable. how are mem metrics?
jamie: within 60s of flag flip: eviction rate dropped 70% on embeddings route, free_slots rose from 120 -> 1400, arena malloc failures decreased in logs
ops-bot: [INCIDENT] Status update posted to #incidents. severity: high, impact: degraded throughput for select customers, mitigation in flight
maria-cs: telling affected customers we have a mitigation applied and are monitoring; no SLA breach yet but we're watching. asking for a small credit preemptively
leo: pushing the small-slot-first eviction canary config: ```
PATCH /internal/kvcache/config
{ "shard":"shard-1","eviction_policy":"small-first","canary":true }
```
leo: canary OK after 5m, eviction churn reduced, p99 latency starting to come down
devin: good. next step: revert the continuous-batching auto-tuner change that shipped yesterday to avoid recurrence. who owns that PR?
jamie: PR #4823 by infra-batching-team — it changed growth heuristics to be too aggressive with multi-seq requests. tagging infra-batching-team now: @infra-batching-team
anya: i'm posting a quick hotfix rollback to revert the growth heuristic while we do a deeper postmortem
devin: go for rollback and keep the runtime overrides in place until we validate the allocator improvements
leo: rollback drafted, executing: ```
git revert --no-edit a12b9f6
bazel run //infra/continuous-batching:deploy --env=prod-us-west-2 --tag=rollback-2026-03-15
```
leo: deploy succeeded to 100% in 4m. rolling metrics show steady decline in large batch occurrences
jamie: allocator logs now: ```
2026-03-15T19:46:01Z  [arena] alloc ok
2026-03-15T19:46:05Z  [kv-cache] slab_fragmentation=0.31 free_slots=4200 used_slots=4200
```
maria-cs: customers report improvement, CS will keep 1:1 thread open for the next 2 hours
ops-bot: [RESOLVE] Incident mitigation complete, monitoring 60m for regression. Incident channel pinned with runbook links and checklist
anya: postmortem owners: devin (oncall), jamie (allocator), leo (config), infra-batching-team (root cause). Initial blameless timeline + action items:
- immediate: keep runtime overrides for 24h (leo)
- short: revert permanent change, add safety caps and better canary metrics to continuous-batching autotuner (infra-batching-team)
- medium: add allocator telemetry for fragmentation heatmaps per shard and automatic compaction trigger (jamie)
- long: improve e2e tests for mixed-sequence workloads to catch batch growth pathologies (devin)
maria-cs: request to add an internal incident note for impacted customers + suggested credits and communications template
devin: creating postmortem ticket INF-2026-451 and assigning owners. Will schedule 1hr sync in 90m to review telemetry and next steps
jamie: thanks team. leaving a short note in the runbook about the specific config keys used and why we prefer max_items cap over unbounded growth
leo: cleaning up canaries, leaving overrides for 24h as requested
anya: good job all. closing active pager — will reopen if any spike within the monitoring window :thumbsup:
ops-bot: [LOG] incident closed by devin at 2026-03-15T20:12:10Z
